question.text: Options strategies result in nonlinear payoffs because:

answer.text: The optionality gives the buyer the right without obligation — limited downside but unlimited/high upside
Exchanges apply different margin rates at different price levels
The underlying commodity has seasonal price patterns

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the option buyer has the right but not the obligation, with downside limited to the premium and upside that is unlimited (for calls) or capped at strike-minus-premium (for puts). This kinked payoff is nonlinear, unlike the straight-line payoff of futures. The Trap: Mathematical formulas describe pricing but do not create the payoff shape. Margins and seasonality do not change the payoff structure. Note: The nonlinearity comes directly from the optionality (right vs obligation), not from any market-structure effect.
